units.translation: A word not read elsewhere, which the scholiast explains as τοῖς πρότερον ἐσχηκόσι δόμον [to those who formerly had a house]. νῦν γὰρ οὐκ εἰσὶ δό-μοι · φρούδα γὰρ ἤδη τάδε [for now there are no houses; for these things are already gone], which are the words of Euripides Med. 139. In M the gloss ἱκέταις [suppliants] is written above. The scholiast's interpretation is correct. Blomfield understands it of the defenders of the house.
and the graces are likewise called a glorious lament for the Atreidae who stand before the house
